def test_odd_count():
    # Single string with multiple odd digits
    assert odd_count(['1234567']) == ["the number of odd elements 4n the str4ng 4 of the 4nput."]

    # Multiple strings with different odd counts
    assert odd_count(['3', '11111111']) == [
        "the number of odd elements 1n the str1ng 1 of the 1nput.",
        "the number of odd elements 8n the str8ng 8 of the 8nput."
    ]

    # No odd digits at all
    assert odd_count(['0246']) == ["the number of odd elements 0n the str0ng 0 of the 0nput."]

    # Empty string input yields count of 0
    assert odd_count(['']) == ["the number of odd elements 0n the str0ng 0 of the 0nput."]

    # Empty input list yields empty result
    assert odd_count([]) == []

    # Mixed digits across several strings
    assert odd_count(['271', '137', '314']) == [
        "the number of odd elements 2n the str2ng 2 of the 2nput.",
        "the number of odd elements 3n the str3ng 3 of the 3nput.",
        "the number of odd elements 2n the str2ng 2 of the 2nput."
    ]

    # Result length matches input length
    assert len(odd_count(['1', '22', '333', '4444'])) == 4

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_odd_count()
